key: And when any one bringeth a meal-offering unto the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon.
s: After the burnt-offerings, the law turns to the offering of flour; Rashi, on 2:1, reads nefesh, soul, rendered ‘any one’, as the poor man who usually brings it, counted by God as though he offered his soul, and Ibn Ezra, on 2:1, as naming the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill gift and the soul too is called willing.
src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Leviticus 2:1, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: לֹא נֶאֱמַר נֶפֶשׁ בְּכָל קָרְבְּנוֹת נְדָבָה אֶלָּא בַּמִּנְחָה, מִי דַּרְכּוֹ לְהִתְנַדֵּב מִנְחָה? עָנִי. אָמַר הַקָּבָּ"ה, מַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עָלָיו כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרִיב נַפְשׁוֹ … נפש אדם והזכיר הנפש שהמנחה נדבה גם הנפש תקרא נדיבה ורוח נדיבה תסמכני
evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 2:1, ‘and when a soul offers’:] Nefesh is not said of any freewill offering except the meal-offering. Who usually volunteers a meal-offering? The poor man. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I account it to him as though he offered his soul … [Ibn Ezra on 2:1, same words:] Nefesh means a person; and it names the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill offering, and the soul too is called willing: ‘and let a willing spirit uphold me’.

reason: The problem holds: ‘as the soul named because this is a freewill gift’ reads as a noun with a participle and ‘this’ lacks a clear antecedent. Re-opened packet.js tanakh 31 --verse 2:1: Ibn Ezra on ונפש כי תקריב, ‘נפש אדם והזכיר הנפש שהמנחה נדבה גם הנפש תקרא נדיבה ורוח נדיבה תסמכני’: it names the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill gift, and the soul too is called willing. The half now reads ‘as naming the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill gift and the soul too is called willing’, which is his wording (והזכיר, המנחה, גם) and no more.
